title: Structure à l'infini des Mg,ν [pages 1 à 90, dont table des matières] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context, from the surrounding pages: these notes study the 'structure at infinity' of the moduli spaces M_{g,ν}. The aim is to describe the fundamental groupoid near the boundary combinatorially.

Setup carried over from (210)–(211):
- D_{d0,...,dr} are boundary-type strata indexed by decreasing sequences d0 ≥ d1 ≥ ... ≥ dr.
- D* denotes the open part of each stratum.
- G is a torus-type group over D, and P is a G-torsor. Concretely, P is the punctured tubular / normal neighbourhood, whose fibres are products of punctured discs or C*'s.
- T is the local system, a twisted Z^{d0}, of π1 (or equivalently H1) of the fibres of P.
- Everything is bundled over the symbols Δ_r as disjoint unions: D_{Δr} = ⊔ D_{d0..dr}, and similarly G_{Δr}, P_{Δr}, T_{Δr}.

On this page:
- (212) defines Π_{Δr} := Π1(D*_{Δr}), the fundamental groupoid of the open strata, and Π̃_{Δr} := Π1(P*_{Δr}), the fundamental groupoid of the punctured tubular neighbourhoods.
- (213) says the projection P* → D* induces a functor Π̃_{Δr} → Π_{Δr}. This makes Π̃ a groupoid extension of Π by the local system T_{Δr} (more precisely T*_{Δr}). In other words, π1 of the punctured neighbourhood of a stratum is an extension of π1 of the open stratum by the free abelian group generated by loops around the d0 branches meeting there.
- (214), noted 'pour mémoire': both groupoids decompose as disjoint unions over d0 ≥ ... ≥ dr. The local system T_{Δr} correspondingly splits into the pieces T_{d0...dr}.
- Final remark: the Π_{Δr} do NOT depend simplicially on Δ_r in the naive way. For example, there is no natural morphism between Π_{d,d'} = Π1 D*_{d,d'} and Π_{d'} = Π1 D*_{d'}. By contrast (next page), there is one between Π_{d,d'} and Π_d.
- The next page makes this precise. Maps α: Δ_r → Δ_{r'} with α(0) = 0 induce finite étale maps D_{Δr'} → D_{Δr}, hence 2-cartesian squares of groupoids. Grothendieck himself calls all this formal and trivial.

Modern reading: for M_{g,ν} this is the classical description of the stabilizer of a multicurve σ in the mapping class group. That stabilizer is an extension of the mapping class group of the cut surface (up to finite symmetries) by the free abelian group Z^σ of Dehn twists, organised over the poset/simplicial structure of the curve complex. The open strata are orbifold K(π,1)'s, which is what makes the extension exact.
errors: Exactness of 1 → T → Π̃ → Π → 1 needs the boundary map π2(D*) → π1(fibre) to vanish. For a general torus torsor this can fail (e.g. a C*-bundle of nonzero Chern class over P^1). The margin of the previous page ('π2(D_{d0..dr}) = 0') shows Grothendieck was aware of this. For moduli strata it holds because they are orbifold K(π,1)'s, but the page states the extension without the hypothesis.
The page writes the kernel as T_{Δr}, but it should strictly be the restriction T*_{Δr} to D*_{Δr}. This is notational only.

ideas.what: π1 of the punctured tubular neighbourhood of a boundary stratum is an extension of π1 of the open stratum by a twisted Z^d of 'loops at infinity'
ideas.modern_name: Stabilizer of a multicurve as an extension by the Dehn-twist group Z^σ; local fundamental group at the boundary of a normal-crossings/toroidal compactification
ideas.usually_credited_to: Birman–Lubotzky–McCarthy, Ivanov (1980s) for mapping class groups; Deligne/SGA7-style tame fundamental group for normal crossings
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme alludes to the structure at infinity and the Teichmüller tower without this formalism; SGA1 XIII has tame π1 of normal crossings

ideas.what: Packaging the strata, torsors and groupoids over Δ_r as disjoint unions indexed by d0 ≥ ... ≥ dr, with only partial simplicial functoriality (maps fixing 0, which are finite étale)
ideas.modern_name: Stratified fundamental groupoid / diagram of groupoids over the boundary complex (dual complex, curve complex)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Harvey, Ivanov, and later work on Teichmüller towers (Lochak–Schneps, Nakamura) and exit-path categories

deep.surprise_reason: This is a routine formal setup: an extension of fundamental groupoids for punctured normal bundles of strata. It matches well-known descriptions of multicurve stabilizers, and Grothendieck himself calls it 'formal and trivial'.
transcription_corrections: (214): the indexing is d0 ≥ d1 ≥ ... ≥ dr (non-strict), not d0 > d1 > ... > dr.

The last paragraph reads 'Les Π_{Δr} n'ont pas de "dépendance simpliciale" p.r. aux Δr, p.ex. on n'a pas de morphismes naturels entre Π_{d,d'} = Π1 D*_{d,d'} et Π_{d'} = Π1 D*_{d'}, [par contre ...]'. This is a negative statement, consistent with the next page's 'par contre il y a ... entre Π_{d,d'} et Π_d'.
(212) margin: 'groupoïde fond. de D*_{Δr} et de P*_{Δr}'.
